title: My Thoughts on Awful Subjects Roll
description: My Thoughts on Awful Subjects Roll in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 2, headed “The death of a sinner”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: My thoughts on aw-ful sub-jects roll, Dam-na-tion and the dead; What hor-rors seize the guilt-y soul Up-on a dy-ing bed!

lines: My thoughts on awful subjects roll,
What horrors seize the guilty soul
Till like a flood with rapid force
Then swift and dreadful she descends
There endless crowds of sinners lie,
Tortur'd with keen despair they cry,
Not all their anguish and their blood
Nor the compassions of a God
Amazing grace, that kept my breath,
Till I had learn'd my Saviour's death,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
